newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shortlists five advisers in telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shortlists five advisers in telecom sale.

text.p: Jordan's profitable state telecommunications monopoly has shortlisted five foreign financial consultants to help it divest a 26 percent stake to a strategic partner by the end of next year.
Minister of Communications Jamal Sarayrah said in a statement on Sunday he expected that winner to be picked by the end of the year. A total of 19 firms had applied.
The firm chosen will help advise the government on all aspects related to the sale of the key divestiture in the wholly state-owned Jordan Telecommunications Company.

The move is a test of the seriousness of government pledges to step up a programme to sell profitable majority state-owned concerns under a privatisation plan key to the success of IMF-guided economic reforms.
The offers reflected strong foreign investor interest in the telecommunications sector Sarayra added, saying he expected the tender for the strategic partner to attract equally strong interest.
He did not give an exact date but said the sale should be completed by end of 1997.

A telecommunications law passed last year set up a regulatory body in charge of overseeing the telecommunications sector, with powers to regulate pricing and licensing of private companies operating in the sector.

Industry officials say the telecoms business in Jordan offers huge potential in a country with 350,00 telephone numbers in a population of over four million. The government has begun awarding tenders since 1994 in a project to add an extra 440,000 telephone lines by 1998.
